title: Not All Prefills Are Equal: PPD Disaggregation for Multi-turn LLM Serving
technique: Prefill-Prefill-capable-Decode (PPD): per-request routing of Turn 2+ append-prefill to the decode node (using cached KV) vs the prefill node, chosen by sign of S = w_ttft·ΔTTFT − w_tpot·ΔTPOT from an offline lookup table

optimized_metrics.evidence: we score the benefit of local processing (x=1) over the PD path (x=0) for workload ψ as ... where ∆ttft is the relative TTFT improvement
∆tpot the relative TPOT degradation when ψ is processed locally rather than through P.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: We measure Turn 1 TTFT, Turn 2 TTFT, average TPOT, throughput (tokens/sec), and success rate.

headline_claim.text: PPD reduces Turn 2+ time-to-first-token (TTFT) by ∼68% while maintaining competitive time-per-output-token (TPOT), effectively alleviating KV transfer congestion under high load.

reported_metrics.where: Table 2, Fig 1 TPS; paper: 'Throughput is a system-level emergent metric and is not optimized per-request'
Fig 1, Fig 9 (P99 TTFT vs TPS Pareto frontiers); not in the routing objective
Fig 4 average query latency vs QPS (15-25% reduction), Fig 5
success rate = share of requests completing without timeout (>=95%), 30 s timeout

metric_definitions.definition_quote: success rate (defined as ≥95% of requests completing without timeout)
metric_definitions.notes: Service degradation = success rate <95%; 30 s timeout. Not a latency SLO.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We measure Turn 1 TTFT, Turn 2 TTFT, average TPOT, throughput (tokens/sec), and success rate.
metric_definitions.notes: TTFT and TPOT never formally defined (TTFT only introduced as 'time-to-first-token'); throughput in tokens/sec, input/output counting unspecified. TTFT reported per turn; statistic for TTFT not stated (appears mean) except P99 in Fig 1.

slo_spec: No numeric SLO; operator weights (w_ttft, w_tpot) act as the SLO knob; paper says PPD 'does not enforce end-to-end SLO bounds' and suggests higher-level controllers drive w from observed P99.
load_regime: Poisson conversation arrivals at target QPS (0.5-20), 10 s fixed-duration test points; ShareGPT and WildChat multi-turn; synthetic sweeps
tradeoff_acknowledged: TTFT vs TPOT: full AP-to-D (x=1) gives 94-96% Turn 2+ TTFT reduction with 7-12% TPOT degradation; no static x wins all objectives (92.2% of workload-QPS combos differ between TTFT and TPOT winners).
hardware: 4x NVIDIA H100 80GB node (network slowdown emulated for multi-node)
workloads: ShareGPT, WildChat multi-turn; synthetic prefill-/decode-heavy mixes
extractor_notes: TAIL IN OBJECTIVE: no. The routing score uses relative TTFT/TPOT improvement from offline measurements at x=0 and x=1; P99 TTFT appears only in the Pareto plots (Fig 1, 9) and as a proposed input to an external controller. Statistic of the TTFT in the score is not stated. 'Weights' are an operator trade-off knob (TTFT vs TPOT) rather than an SLO threshold.
load_class_quote: conversations arriving according to a Poisson process at the target QPS (e.g., QPS=4 generates ∼40 two-turn conversations).
